title: Linux.Ngioweb_Botnet_Investigation_75a
description: Investigate and respond to unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents caused by the Linux.Ngioweb botnet.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and respond to these issues.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim machine with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: investigator
- Password: SecurePass123!

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim machine with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: investigator
- Password: SecurePass123!

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is beaconing to an external command-and-control server?
levels.solution: Check running services and look for unusual network connections. The suspicious service is likely named `malicious-beacon.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and look for unusual network connections.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or those that are not part of the standard system services.

levels.title: Identify Flood Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service generating the flood of network traffic?
levels.solution: Investigate systemd timers and services that might be responsible for network flooding. The service is likely named `malicious-flood.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd timers and services that might be responsible for network flooding.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that are triggering services with unusual names.

levels.title: Identify Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the systemd timer responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Look for systemd timers that might be triggering the suspicious service. The timer is likely named `malicious-update.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for systemd timers that might be triggering the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that are triggering services with unusual names.
